ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $7.12 Ryde voucher (voucher form under NS-7) as the refund for the non-exempt off-route segment F4
ruling.reasoning:
The trip was RydeTAXI, metered [F8], so extra kilometres enter the fare and RD-2's metered branch governs: the refund is Σ(extra_km of non-exempt segments) × this trip's per-km rate [RD-2]. The rate is the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km: $29.44 ÷ 20.88 km = $1.4100/km [F5][F8][RD-2]. There is exactly one off-route segment, F4 (14:33–14:48, 7.45 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.40 km, +5.05 km, up to 1987 m off the corridor) [F4][RD-1].

RD-5 consent: before the segment began at 14:33 the rider wrote at 14:30 "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late." [F10][F4]. Read in context, that is a general route choice, so the segment's finding is "counts" on the ground driver_errand: the driver's own post-trip statement admits "I went round the jam and stopped briefly to collect something on the way" [F12], and the system record places a 4 min 0 s standstill at 14:38–14:42, inside the off-route window and at neither endpoint (7443 m from pickup, 6033 m from drop-off) [F2][F4]. A general authorisation covers the route chosen to get to the destination, not an errand or stop of the driver's own, and a driver's statement of agreement is a claim, not the rider's consent; the rider named no place, so RD-3(a) gives no exemption for the stop either [F12][F10][F2][RD-5][RD-3][G11].

The amount therefore follows the trace formula: 5.05 km × $1.4100/km = $7.1205, rounded to $7.12 [F4][F5][RD-2]. The $1.15 waiting item [F6] is a metered waiting unit on this RydeTAXI trip, not a "fee_waived" supplementary charge of the kind NS-6 governs, and it is not part of the trace's distance formula, so it is not added: any waiver of that item under RD-3(c)/NS-6 must go to a human, which is why the refund is $7.12 and not more [F6][F2][RD-2][RD-3].

RD-6 does not fire: the trace settles route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so the "repeated" condition is not met and no account flag is warranted, notwithstanding the 4 disputes / 2 upheld in 90 days at F19 [F19][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages [F9][F10], the driver statement [F12] and the traffic records [F13][F14][F15][F16] — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; this is a fare-and-route dispute only [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence is sufficient: the GPS segment and stop, the fare breakdown and rate, and a complete, fully timestamped two-message chat [F11] settle every element this ruling needs [RD-2][RD-5][G12].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's only pre-segment message, F10 sent 14:30 before the 14:33 segment start [F4], is a general route choice ('Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late') [RD-5]: it covers the route chosen to reach the destination, not an errand of the driver's own. The driver's own post-trip statement F12 admits 'I went round the jam and stopped briefly to collect something on the way', and the system record F2 places a 4 min 0 s standstill at 14:38–14:42 inside the off-route window, 7443 m from pickup and 6033 m from drop-off — a stop away from the route that no rider message asked for [F2][F4]. A driver's statement of agreement is not the rider's consent, and the rider named no place, so RD-3(a) does not exempt the stop [G11][RD-3]. The segment counts; its extra_km are refundable: 5.05 km × $1.4100/km = $7.12 [F4][F5][RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: A general route delegation ('Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late', F10) sent before the segment start [F4] does not exempt the whole segment: the driver's own statement F12 admits he 'stopped briefly to collect something on the way', and the system record F2 places a 4 min 0 s standstill inside the off-route window at neither endpoint, which a general authorisation does not cover [RD-5]. The segment counts.

The Central Expressway band-2 record F13 covers only 14:11–14:33 and is corroborative at most; no traffic incident was recorded on the route during the trip window [F16], so RD-4(b) alone cannot exempt, and F13 does not explain the segment running to 14:48 up to 1987 m off the corridor [F4][RD-4].

Base, distance, time and platform components are ordinary metered items, but the excess distance item is not untouchable: the trace shows one off-route segment [F4] whose extra_km are refundable under RD-2, priced at the fare record's rate $29.44 ÷ 20.88 km = $1.4100/km [F5][F8][RD-2].

The absence of a road name for the driven path does not save the segment; the finding rests on the general-consent branch read with the driver's admitted errand [F10][F12][RD-5], so no named road is needed for the segment to count.

F5's $7.46 is priced on the measured overall excess of 5.29 km, which is not the non-exempt segment's extra_km. RD-2 refunds the non-exempt segment's extra_km, and F4 records +5.05 km, so the refundable distance item is 5.05 km × $1.4100/km = $7.12, not $7.46 [F4][F5][RD-2].

The rider requests the $1.15 waiting item be refunded alongside the distance; it is a metered waiting unit on this RydeTAXI trip [F6][RD-2], not a supplementary charge waivable under RD-3(c)/NS-6, so it falls outside the trace's distance formula and is not added to the award — a waiver of it must go to a human [F6][F2][RD-2][RD-3].
